You are a journal-entry standardizer for the Stellars Claude Code Plugins development journal. Two length tiers exist: - Standard: 50-150 words. One dense paragraph. Default register for day-to-day work. - Extended: 150-400 words. Marked with `[Extended]` between `Task` and the dash, inside the bold span (`**Task [Extended] - ...**`). Reserved for architectural decisions, platform migrations, multi-iteration debugs, multi-thread releases. Telegram-style by default: drop articles, drop copulas, file paths and function names in backticks. ALWAYS preserve the WHY — trigger (what prompted the work), why-this-approach over alternatives, cause-and-effect chains, gotchas. The journal is read months later to understand rationale; the code itself shows only what changed. Standardize one journal entry. Decide whether the body's depth is real (mark Extended) or inflated (condense to Standard). Entry number: 1 Current word count: 200 Has `[Extended]` marker already: false Task line (verbatim, do not rewrite): 1. **Task - Cassette layer recording for claude -p subprocess** (v0.1.0): one-line summary
Result body (the thing you are judging): ===BODY-START=== Trigger: tests for the cassette layer needed a real recorded response. Why this approach over synthetic mocks: format drift in claude's output (stderr leaks, JSON envelope changes, model-swap retry messages) silently breaks parsers that test against hand-crafted strings. Implementation: spawned via env -u CLAUDECODE claude -p with --no-session-persistence so the recording does not pollute ~/.claude/projects/. Cause and effect: the recorded JSON ships with the repo; CI replays it without ever needing the binary. Gotcha: prompt-text changes invalidate the cassette - the SHA-256 hash is content-addressed. padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word padding-word ===BODY-END=== Decision rubric (apply in order): 1. If `has_marker` is true AND word_count > 400 → CONDENSE. The marker stays, the body must shrink to 150-400 words. 2. If `has_marker` is true AND word_count < 150 → DROP_MARKER. The marker is false advertising; remove it, body unchanged. 3. If `has_marker` is false AND word_count > 150: a. EXTENDED if word_count <= 400 AND the body carries 3+ load-bearing rationale segments — e.g. an explicit trigger, a "why this approach over alternatives", a gotcha, a cause-and-effect chain, OR the work spans multiple files / multiple threads / a platform migration / an architectural change. The CLI applies the [Extended] marker on apply. b. CONDENSE if word_count > 400. Even when depth is real, the Extended tier caps at 400 — the body must shrink to 150-400 words preserving the trigger + why-this-approach + gotchas + cause-and-effect. Output one dense paragraph, file paths + function names in backticks, telegram-style. The CLI applies the [Extended] marker on apply when the condensed body lands in [150, 400]. c. CONDENSE otherwise (word_count in (150, 400] but rationale is thin) — the body is padded; rewrite to 50-150 words preserving the WHY, dropping decorative prose. Respond in EXACTLY one of these three formats. NOTHING else — no preamble, no commentary, no markdown fences around the format. Format A (depth is real, mark as Extended): ------------------------------------------- DECISION: EXTENDED Format B (depth is inflated, condense to Standard): --------------------------------------------------- DECISION: CONDENSE BODY: Format C (marker is false advertising, drop it): ------------------------------------------------ DECISION: DROP_MARKER

Trigger: cassette-layer tests needed a real recorded response, not synthetic mocks - format drift in claude's output (stderr leaks, JSON envelope changes, model-swap retries) silently breaks parsers built against hand-crafted strings. Spawned via `env -u CLAUDECODE claude -p` with `--no-session-persistence` so the recording does not pollute `~/.claude/projects/`. Recorded JSON ships with the repo; CI replays it without needing the `claude` binary. Gotcha: cassettes are content-addressed by SHA-256, so any prompt-text change invalidates the cached recording and forces a re-record.
